solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: One venomous corner not half welcomed by the Kop

indicators.note: welcomed by means the shortened corner goes inside the other piece

parts.note: Spion Kop is the South African hill whose name was given to Liverpool's Kop terrace

indicators.note: not half means only the first half of corner is kept

parts.note: the word corner itself, of which half is used

explanation.surface: A football picture: a corner kick and the Kop end at Anfield, Liverpool's ground.
explanation.walkthrough: Liverpool's Kop stand was named after the Boer War battle of Spion Kop, so the Kop gives the hill's first name; corner keeps only its first three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A scorpion is an arachnid with a venomous sting in its tail.

clue.text: Market is very British

parts.note: so means very, as in 'so good'
the United Kingdom

explanation.surface: A trader boasts that the market is thoroughly British.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads like a boast about a market's Britishness, but it splits cleanly into a definition and two short pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A souk is an open-air bazaar in an Arab or North African town, a trading place with stalls.

clue.text: Most half-hearted moving around, but he keeps rolling

indicators.note: things that move around are shifted about, so the letters change places

parts.note: all fifteen letters used as they stand

explanation.surface: A lazy, listless person drifting about, contrasted with someone who keeps on rolling.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole of 'Most half-hearted' is the fodder, not a hint to drop a middle letter. The Thames is London's river, personified as Old Father Thames.
explanation.definitionFit: The personified river flows on without stopping, echoing the song line about a river that just keeps rolling along.

clue.text: Herb's wallet nearly getting dropped on road

indicators.note: in a down clue, dropped on means placed on top of, so the road comes below
nearly means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a purse is a wallet for money
a lane is a narrow road

explanation.surface: A herbalist's wallet nearly lost when dropped in the road.
explanation.definitionFit: Purslane is a succulent plant used as a salad herb and vegetable.

clue.text: Down; unable to fly with this?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: in debt, as in being down money
second meaning, read cryptically: O for nothing plus WING, a bird with no wing

explanation.walkthrough: Down suggests feathers, which leads towards birds; really it means owing money. The second half splits as O (zero) plus WING, and the question mark flags that pun.
explanation.definitionFit: To be down on a bet or account is to be in debt, still having money to repay.

clue.text: Legendary footballers having brief time with our team

parts.note: the Football Association, English football's governing body
a mo is a moment, short for a brief spell
our side is us

explanation.surface: Star footballers of old spend a short while playing for our side.
explanation.walkthrough: The FA is the Football Association, which runs English football; 'mo' is British slang for a moment.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone legendary is renowned and widely celebrated, so the two adjectives are close synonyms.

clue.text: Zero interest each year closing course

indicators.note: to close around something is to shut it inside

parts.note: as in ten pounds a head
the abbreviation for year
a path is a course or route

explanation.surface: A loan offering no interest in any year until the course of repayment closes.
explanation.walkthrough: Zero interest reads as a finance term; it is the definition, meaning no enthusiasm at all. A and Y together close around the course.
explanation.definitionFit: Apathy is a lack of concern or enthusiasm, the complete absence of caring about something.

clue.text: Comment on letters for military checkpoint

parts.note: a remark or comment
letters delivered are the post

explanation.surface: Someone writes remarks on correspondence meant for an army checkpoint.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer, the comment sits on top of the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An observation post is a military position from which troops watch enemy movements, a manned lookout station.

clue.text: Great changes in view left to those eg in the circle

definitions.text: left to those eg in the circle

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters within the word for view

parts.note: a sight is a view

indicators.note: changes means the letters of great are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sweeping change to the view from the theatre seats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' looks like part of the wordplay; it starts the definition. The circle is an upper tier of theatre seats, facing the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Stage right is the actor's right, which is the audience's left as they look at the stage.

clue.text: Hitch as part of sail lands on shorebird

indicators.note: in a down answer, what lands on something rests above it

parts.note: a reef is the part of a sail that can be rolled up to reduce its area
the knot is a small wading sandpiper

explanation.surface: A snag as a torn piece of sail comes down on a bird at the water's edge.
explanation.walkthrough: Hitch reads as a hold-up, but it is the sailor's word for a knot tying a rope.
explanation.definitionFit: A hitch is a kind of knot used to fasten rope, and this square knot is one used for tying reefs.

clue.text: Stress of old pants etc being a bit short

indicators.note: something a bit short is lacking a little at its end, so the final letter goes

parts.note: an old-fashioned word for underwear, pants included

explanation.surface: The worry of worn-out underwear that no longer quite fits.
explanation.walkthrough: In British English pants are underpants, and underlinen is a dated word for underclothes; drop its last N.
explanation.definitionFit: To underline a point is to emphasise it, just as to stress it; both are verbs of emphasis.

clue.text: Articles about poet initially bewildered

indicators.note: to be about something is to surround it

parts.note: two indefinite articles
the initials of the poet Thomas Stearns Eliot

explanation.surface: Pieces of writing about a poet leave the reader confused from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Initially' looks like a first-letter signal, which would give P; instead it asks for the poet's initials, T S E for T. S. Eliot.
explanation.definitionFit: Being at sea is an idiom for being confused and lost, like a sailor without land in sight.

clue.text: Follow story as told

indicators.note: something told is spoken, so it is the sound that counts

parts.note: a tale is a story

explanation.surface: An instruction to go along with a story just as it was recounted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Follow' looks like it goes with 'story' as in following a plot, but it stands alone as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To tail someone is to follow them closely and secretly, as a detective shadows a suspect.

clue.text: Showing amazing foresight, a present not to be criticised

definitions.text: a present not to be criticised

indicators.note: to amaze is to confound, so the letters are thrown into confusion

parts.note: used as it stands, all nine letters

explanation.surface: Choosing a flawless gift in advance shows remarkable foresight.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb says never look a gift horse in the mouth: do not find fault with something given to you.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb warns against inspecting a donated horse's teeth for its age, so it stands for any gift one should accept uncritically.

clue.text: Ingratiating European put out by old uniform in funeral ceremony

indicators.note: put out by means one letter is ejected and others take its place

parts.note: obsequies are funeral rites
U is uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A European mourner made to leave a funeral by an old man in uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: The second E of OBSEQUIES, the one before S, is the one replaced by OU.
explanation.definitionFit: Obsequious behaviour is fawning and servile, trying to win favour by flattery.

clue.text: Where it is polite to cough, if late

definitions.text: Where it is polite to cough
definitions.meaning: first meaning, split in two: good manners say cover your mouth, so you cough behind a hand
second meaning: behind schedule, in arrears

explanation.surface: Etiquette advice on where to cough if you arrive late somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half is a playful reading of the word as two, behind plus hand; the second half is its ordinary sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Being behindhand means running late or falling behind with payments or work.

clue.text: Indicate tune of one song half-heartedly — it is rather wet

parts.note: to hum a tune is to indicate it without words
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: half-heartedly means one of the two middle letters of the word is lost

parts.note: a ditty is a short simple song

explanation.surface: Someone humming a song half-heartedly while it drizzles.
explanation.walkthrough: DITTY has TT at its heart; losing half of it leaves DITY.
explanation.definitionFit: Humidity is moisture in the air, so a humid day is damp and close.

clue.text: A little animal in the country

indicators.note: only a little of the words is taken, a short run from inside them

parts.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: A small creature living out in the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The country' looks like the rural countryside; it is a nation, found straddling 'animal in'.
explanation.definitionFit: Mali is a landlocked West African nation whose capital is Bamako.

clue.text: Elephant keeps quiet, with a series of gestures

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it, so one piece holds another

parts.note: Dumbo is the flying elephant of the Disney film
the call for silence
the abbreviation for with

explanation.surface: An elephant stays silent and communicates by miming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' looks like a link word but supplies the final W.
explanation.definitionFit: A dumbshow is a performance in mime, communicating by gestures and expressions without speaking.

clue.text: Seizure regularly downed a biblical figure

indicators.note: to down something is to swallow it, so one part takes on the next
at regular intervals, so every other letter is taken

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone having a fit collapses at the sight of a figure from the Bible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Downed' looks like knocked over, but it means swallowed, the alternate letters taking in the A.
explanation.definitionFit: Ezra is the Old Testament scribe and priest who led Jews back from Babylon and gives his name to a book.

clue.text: Expression of surprise about colleague Leon maybe being clumsy

indicators.note: about means the exclamation goes around the other pieces

parts.note: ah is an expression of surprise
a mate is a colleague, a workmate
Leon Uris was the American novelist who wrote Exodus; maybe flags him as one example of a Leon

explanation.surface: Surprise at how ham-fisted a colleague called Leon is.
explanation.definitionFit: Amateurish work lacks professional skill, so it is clumsy or inept.

clue.text: Clumsy cowboy endlessly on tablet

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above, so the tablet comes after
endlessly means the last letter of the word is cut

parts.note: a gaucho is a South American cowboy
E is slang for an ecstasy tablet

explanation.surface: An awkward cowboy whose story goes on and on, taking a pill.
explanation.definitionFit: Gauche means socially awkward and lacking grace, so clumsy in manner.

clue.text: Superior forehand smashes outrageous

parts.note: U means upper-class, as in U and non-U

indicators.note: something smashed is broken into pieces and scattered

parts.note: the eight letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A tennis player's superb forehand smashes are shocking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smashes' sounds like a tennis shot beside 'forehand', but it is the anagram signal. U for upper-class is an old British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unheard-of is unprecedented and shocking, so extreme that it is scandalous.

clue.text: A young deer we hear leading all the animals around

indicators.note: what leads goes first, ahead of the rest
what we hear is spoken, so sound matters rather than spelling

parts.note: a fawn is a young deer; a faun is a woodland spirit
taken as written

explanation.surface: A young deer is said to lead all the other animals in the area.
explanation.walkthrough: The spoken fawn is spelt as faun, the goat-legged spirit of Roman myth, and it leads the A.
explanation.definitionFit: Fauna is the collective term for the animal life of a particular region or period.

clue.text: Spy, English — or Flemish?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: James, the fictional secret agent 007
second meaning: two patterns of laying bricks in a wall

explanation.walkthrough: The surface asks whether a spy is English or Flemish; in bricklaying, English and Flemish are two named patterns of courses, and the question mark marks them as examples.
explanation.definitionFit: The fictional agent is James Bond, and in masonry a bond is the arrangement in which bricks overlap.

clue.text: In crush, losing top part of foot

indicators.note: in a down answer the top is the first letter, and losing it removes that letter

parts.note: being in a crush is being in a pinch, a tight squeeze

explanation.surface: Someone caught in a crowd loses their shoe and hurts their foot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part of foot' looks like toe or heel; it is the unit of length, a twelfth of a foot.
explanation.definitionFit: A foot measures twelve inches, so an inch is one fraction of that imperial length.

clue.text: Universal at first to suffer loss of smell

indicators.note: losing something at the start means the opening letter goes

parts.note: cosmic means relating to the universe

explanation.surface: Everyone is at first bound to lose their sense of smell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loss of smell' reads as a phrase, but the break comes after 'loss'; 'of smell' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Osmic is a rare adjective relating to odours or the olfactory sense, from the Greek word for scent.

clue.text: Land in built-up area — it hurt duke to divide that

indicators.note: to divide that means these pieces split the built-up area in two, sitting inside it

parts.note: a town is a built-up area
ouch is what you say when it hurt

explanation.surface: A duke landing in a town and complaining of the pain of splitting it.
explanation.walkthrough: Land looks like a noun, ground or territory; it is the verb, as an aircraft lands. That refers back to the built-up area, which the cry of pain and the duke split.
explanation.definitionFit: To touch down is to land, as an aircraft does on a runway.

clue.text: Not popular, one demanding hospital post

indicators.note: not having something means it is left out

parts.note: one who insists
in fashion is popular

explanation.surface: An unpopular applicant who keeps demanding a job at the hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: The demander loses the IN at the front. In Britain a sister is a senior nurse in charge of a ward.
explanation.definitionFit: In British hospitals the title is a senior nursing rank, the nurse who runs a ward.

clue.text: Character transported returning from game involving good group of women

indicators.note: involving means the game wraps around the other pieces

parts.note: a match is a game; from just leads into it
the WI, the Women's Institute, is a British women's organisation

explanation.surface: A Women's Institute team returning from a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' looks like a reversal signal; it is part of the definition, since Magwitch returns from Australia. The WI is the Women's Institute, a British community group.
explanation.definitionFit: In Dickens's Great Expectations the convict Magwitch is transported to Australia and secretly comes back.
